The high-energy physics toolkit

From Feynman diagrams
to amplitudes

HEPkit brings together a collection of packages for state-of-the-art particle physics. Generate Feynman diagrams, manipulate tensors, compute loop amplitudes, and reduce integrals in one coherent workflow, powered by Symbolica.

Explore the examplesRead the documentation
From a model to diagramsPython / HEPkit
from symbolica.community import hepkit

# Choose a model and a process.
model = hepkit.Model.qcd()
process = model.process(["g"], ["g"])

# Generate one-loop diagrams.
result = process.generate_diagrams(loops=1)

Packages and contributors

The projects behind HEPkit

HEPkit brings together packages for Feynman diagrams, tensor algebra, and loop integrals.

10 PROJECTS
The computer algebra foundation

Symbolica

The shared engine for symbolic algebra and numerical computation. It connects the packages below and makes them accessible from Python.

AuthorBen Ruijl
ProjectCitation
Models, diagrams & amplitudes

Gammaloop

Particle models and UFO import, Feynman-diagram generation, amplitudes, kinematics, Cross-Free Families, and covariant tensor reduction.

Authors & contributorsValentin Hirschi, Lucien Huber, Mathijs Fraaije, Zeno Capatti
ProjectCredits & citation
Tensor algebra

Spenso

Abstract-index tensors, dense and sparse tensor data, automatic index matching, and tensor-network contractions.

Authors & contributorsLucien Huber
ProjectCredits & citation
Tensor identities

Idenso

Symbolic identities and simplification for Dirac matrices, color structures, metrics, and Levi-Civita tensors. Available through the shared tensor interface.

Authors & contributorsLucien Huber, Ben Ruijl
ProjectCredits & citation
Graph structure & drawing

Linnet

Half-edge graphs, subgraph operations, topology algorithms, layout, and diagram drawing for physics calculations.

Authors & contributorsLucien Huber
ProjectCredits & citation
Graph generation

Graphica

Generation, manipulation, and canonization of graphs with multiple edges and mixed directed and undirected connections.

Authors & contributorsBen Ruijl
ProjectCredits & citation
Integration-by-parts reduction

RustRed

Native parametric and Laporta IBP reduction, connected to HEPkit through a shared integral-family representation.

Authors & contributorsGregor Kälin, and porting work by Valentin Hirschi
ProjectCredits & citation
Symbolic one-loop reduction

one-loop-reduce

Reduces one-loop integral families and scalar-product numerators to scalar master integrals, keeping the spacetime dimension symbolic.

Authors & contributorsElijah Cavan
ProjectCredits & citation
Numerical one-loop integrals

OneLoopMaster

Symbolica expressions and native numerical evaluation for scalar tadpole, bubble, triangle, and box integrals. Based on OneLOop by Andreas van Hameren.

Authors & contributorsAndreas Van Hameren (ported by Valentin Hirschi)
ProjectCredits & citation
Vacuum integrals

Vakint

Canonical matching, tensor reduction, and analytic or numerical evaluation of single-scale vacuum integrals.

Authors & contributorsValentin Hirschi, Ben Ruijl
ProjectCredits & citation

FeynKit, Spenso, Idenso, Linnet, and Vakint are developed in the GammaLoop repository. Package credits follow the upstream citation records; FeynKit and OneLoopMaster currently credit their contributors collectively.

Additional tools and scientific credits

Depending on the selected evaluation method, Vakint can use the following external tools. These have their own installation requirements and citations.

FORM
Symbolic manipulation for selected vacuum-integral backends.
J. Kuipers, T. Ueda, J. A. M. Vermaseren, J. Vollinga.
MATAD
Analytic evaluation of massive tadpoles.
M. Steinhauser.
FMFT
Evaluation of fully massive four-loop tadpoles.
Andrey Pikelner.
pySecDec
Numerical evaluation through sector decomposition.
S. Borowka, G. Heinrich, S. Jahn, S. P. Jones, M. Kerner, J. Schlenk, T. Zirke.

For research, cite the packages and methods used in your calculation. See the Vakint citation registry for backend-specific references.
